mike: Nightly perf dashboard just alerted at 03:12 UTC — 99th pct latency for short sequences jumped from ~80ms to ~420ms across the canary pool :rotating_light:

yasmin: saw that, looks like it's only on canary nodes (us-east-1-c). baseline pools OK :eyes:

runtime-bot: Canary deploy started by @deployer at 03:09 UTC for release/2026-03-17 -> rollout id r2026-317-canary-4

mike: timeline lines up with the canary roll. rollout included PR #6123 (kernel selection heuristic change). any quick sanity checks?

anika: +1 suspecting #6123. it changed the score calc that prefers fused matmul kernels for batch_size > 1 on small sequence lengths. I pushed a quick profiler run on one canary box:

anika: ```
# perf snapshot 03:20 UTC (canary node)
kernel_select_ms: 72.3  # used to be ~1.5ms
avg_batch_size: 6.8  # spiked from 1.2
kv_evictions_per_min: 180  # huge compared to baseline 8
prefetch_misses: 34
```

josh: whoa kernel_select_ms 72ms is the culprit. that explains tail-latency. looks like kernel selector is doing heavy heuristics per-request now instead of cheap table lookup.

yasmin: logs show repeated fallback churn for the same model instance:

yasmin: ```
[03:10:12] WARN runtime.kselector: re-evaluating kernels for model raptor-v1, seq=8, batch=7
[03:10:12] INFO runtime.kselector: chosen kernel=matmul_fused_v2
[03:10:12] WARN runtime.kselector: prefetch failed: cache_miss
[03:10:12] INFO runtime.kselector: fallback to matmul_generic
[03:10:12] WARN runtime.kselector: triggering kv-evict, current-kv-size=124MB
```

anika: that fallback loop + prefetch misses explains the KV thrash. high batch sizes + mis-preferred kernel -> long select time -> more queued requests -> bigger batches -> worse. feedback loop.

mike: is this reproduceable locally? can we run the nightly workload fixture with PR #6123 applied?

josh: yes i spun up a mini canary with the fixture and reproduced: tail latency 450ms on short seqs. i also attached a flamegraph snapshot (trimmed):

josh: ```
Top functions:
- KernelSelector::score_candidate  (46ms)
- KernelSelector::compute_features (18ms)
- schedule_batch_async (12ms)
- KVCache::evict_if_needed (9ms)
```

mike: OK this is a release blocker for canary. two options: revert #6123 or patch selector to short-circuit when seq <= 16 and batch < 4. thoughts? :hammer:

anika: short-circuit seems safe and quick. #6123 intended to prefer fused kernels for throughput, but we didn't account for small-seq microcases. i can open a PR for a fast guard and run canary patch.

yasmin: we should also bisect the exact sub-change in #6123 that introduced the expensive compute (it was 4 commits). if we revert entire PR we lose some throughput gain. prefer fix+canary.

mike: agreed. action items:
- anika -> PR with short-circuit guard + unit test (low risk) (ETA 1h)
- josh -> run bisect to identify commit causing heavy compute (ETA 2h)
- yasmin -> monitor KV eviction / batch-size metrics and mute nightly alerts for canary while we iterate (so we don't get noise)
- runtime-bot -> keep posting rollout state and perf snapshots
deployer-bot: Rollout r2026-317-canary-4 paused by @mike at 03:34 UTC

mike: i'll hold off on full revert for now. if anika's patch doesn't drop the kernel_select_ms below ~5ms we revert. keep updates in this thread. :thumbsup:

anika: opening draft PR now: r2026/6123-fix-shortseq-guard. will run the canary patch after CI.

josh: bisect results so far: commit 9f3b2a7 toggled feature-flag `selective_fused_preference` and added expensive feature extraction. isolating next to confirm.

yasmin: metric note: even after short-circuit we should add a sampling profiler at 1% for canary to catch regressions earlier. I'll open an infra ticket.

mike: thanks team. keep replies short — paste quick numbers. we'll escalate to SRE pager only if patch fails and revert is needed.

runtime-bot: Perf snapshot logging enabled (1% sampling) on canary pool at 03:42 UTC as requested by yasmin.
